section_summary.extract_value: This section explores loneliness as an aversive experience that motivates social connection, distinguishing between transient and chronic forms. Chronic loneliness is described as trapping individuals in negative social cognitions and self-defeating behaviors, leading to significant physical and psychological decline, including links to depression, cardiovascular risks, and mortality. The text highlights that while intermittent loneliness may serve an adaptive purpose, chronic loneliness has unequivocally deleterious impacts on health, noting a gap in research on daily loneliness and self-reported health functioning. No specific studies are presented within this section.
